bench_setup = function() {
	set.seed(20261117)
	n = 100L
	w = rep(c(0, 1), each = n / 2L)
	T_ev = stats::rexp(n, rate = 0.1 * exp(-0.3 * w))
	L = numeric(n); R = numeric(n)
	for (i in seq_len(n)) {
		visits = cumsum(stats::runif(8L, 1, 4))
		before = visits[visits < T_ev[i]]
		after = visits[visits >= T_ev[i]]
		L[i] = if (length(before)) max(before) else 0
		R[i] = if (length(after)) min(after) else Inf
	}
	w_draws = NULL
	list(L = L, R = R, w = w, w_draws = w_draws)
}

notes: Benchmarks part (2) only (part (1), solving once per randomization test, is spec'd under interval-censored-npmle#43925959437.3): one pooled Turnbull NPMLE at n=100 by interval::icfit (self-consistency EM, KKT error < 1e-6) vs icenReg::ic_np (EMICM in C++, internal stopping rule; its tol argument is not passed to the C code), compared as the NPMLE CDF at every finite right endpoint. Both use (L,R] intervals (icfit's Lin/Rin defaults, ic_np B=c(0,1)) and continuous visit times avoid cross-subject endpoint ties; tol 1e-4 absolute on F because the two stopping rules differ and EMICM's is not documented, so a 'not equivalent' verdict here may be a convergence-tolerance artifact rather than a different estimate.
